ATRAH plunges you into the deepest, darkest trenches of the ocean … Designed by Johannes Goupy and Jérémy Ducret, this tactical game for 2 to 4 players perfectly blends set collection, area majority, and a volatile stock market economic engine. 

In the depths of ATRAH, tension is as thick as the abyss itself. To win, you must collect fearsome sea creatures to influence majorities and double your precious points.

But the surface will grant you no respite: move your ship to seize schools of fish and block other players’ paths.
Shape your own destiny each turn by collecting scoring tiles, turning every decision into a tactical trap closing in on your opponents.

—description from the publisher
community_text:
[Rating: 4/10] After 2 games on BGA: Ugly creatures from the deep sea are a cool illustration theme at least since Deep Regrets. I like it! The gameplay felt a little bland to me. I have to choose between three drafting options while taking a range of factors into account: the cards’ point values, their colors, the card effects, their market value, the special tiles, my own tableau, and the other players’ tableaus. That sounds like a lot, but since there are only three drafting options, in most cases, one option quickly stands out. I don’t want to calculate everything exactly anyway, so intuition takes over.

[Rating: 6/10] Quick set collecting game with good artwork. The random card flips can be a little frustrating, sometimes helping your opponent. This one is best for 2 players, otherwise it gets pretty chaotic.

[Rating: 6.5/10] Still trying to figure it out with majorities and abilities   Score 62-63 first game  Digital

[Rating: 7/10] Atrah is a simple set collection / market manipulation game that plays very quickly. On your turn, you take all the fish cards from one of the three columns facing you, resolve their actions, then keep one fish family while sending the rest to the market. Fish have values from 0–3, and collecting enough different values in a family can earn bonus scoring tiles.  Once three piles in the 3x3 grid are empty, your fish score their face value, with the two fish families most represented in the market scoring double.
